question_en:
I am reviewing the project records for experimental aircraft in the diagram. Use the center of each model label as its position. Start from the topmost complete aircraft, then alternate between moving down-left and down-right, beginning down-left. Each time, select the unvisited complete object with the smallest vertical distance; objects cut off at the image edge are not included in the route. Stop when the project page first explicitly records that the aircraft actually completed captive-carry flight(s). Please answer the following questions:

1. In the actual visitation order, which aircraft were reviewed? For each project, is it explicitly recorded that captive-carry flight(s) were actually completed, and should each step continue or stop? Which aircraft is the first to meet the stopping condition?
2. How many different project pages were reviewed in total?

Answer format: Please answer in points numbered (1)–(2); for question 1, use a table to list the aircraft in order, whether the project page explicitly records actual completion, and the "Continue/Stop" judgment, with the first aircraft meeting the condition directly reflected in the stop row; for question 2, provide the total number of pages in text.
answer:
(1)

| Visit Order | Aircraft | Does the project page explicitly record actual completion of captive-carry flight(s)? | Judgment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | X-29 | Not explicitly recorded | Continue |
| 2 | X-Wing | Not explicitly recorded | Continue |
| 3 | X-30 | Not explicitly recorded | Continue |
| 4 | X-31 | Not explicitly recorded | Continue |
| 5 | X-33 | Not explicitly recorded | Continue |
| 6 | X-34 | Yes | Stop |

(2) A total of 6 different project pages were reviewed.
